title.narrative: Technorseve -Stöd till utveckling inom förädlingsindustrin för jordbruk
Technoserve- Support to the agroprocessing industry

description.narrative: The FED Project aims to increase the revenues, marketable output and job security for more than 100 SMEs within Zambias food processing sector. Furthermore, the contribution intends to deepen the SMEs capacity and sustainability, equipping them with technical and business skills in food processing best practices, and improving their access to inputs, new markets and finance through inclusive models. The three specific objectives that will support the overall project goal of A more inclusive SME food processing sector resulting in increased resilience and economic and nutritional benefits for the Bottom of the Pyramid (BOP) particularly women and youth are: 1) Improving sustainability the productivity and profitability of the SMEs/SGBs food processors. 2) Improving the performance of women led or owned food processors SMEs/ SGBs. 3) Improving the market systems service providers capacity to support SME/ SGBs food processors.

Det övergripande målet för FED-projektet är att öka intäkterna och säljbara volymer, samt skapa och/eller behålla jobb för minst 100 små och medelstora företag inom livsmedelstillverkning, varav minst 50 % av dessa företag kommer att ägas av kvinnor. Detta kommer att ske via tre sammankopplade aktiviteter, nämligen:
1) utföra sektorövergripande utbildningar för utvalda små och medelstora företag; 2) erbjuda skräddarsydda affärsplaner och teknisk assistans för utvalda små och medelstora företag; samt 3) förbättra tillgången till finansiering för utvalda små och medelstora företag.
När dessa aktiviteter kombineras så kan effektiviteten, lönsamheten och tillväxten hos små och medelstora företag nom livsmedelsindustri förbättras vilket bidrar till en starkare och mer inkluderande sektor. Preliminärt har TechnoServe visat att de kommer att arbeta med små och medelstora företag som främst kommer från Lusaka, Kopparbältet, centrala samt östra provinserna. Aktiviteter specifikt inom majs- och kassavasektorn kommer att ske i nordvästra och södra provinserna. Det faktiska geografiska verksamhetsområdet kommer att bestämmas under inledningsfasen på sex månader.
Avtalspartnern är TechnoServe som är en ideell internationell utvecklingsorganisation med sitt huvudkontor i USA och ett landskontor i Zambia.
Budgeten för den föreslagna insatsen är 36 miljoner kronor. Projektet kommer att pågå i tre och ett halvt år (42 månader), inklusive en inledningsfas på sex månader. Det kommer inte att vidarebefordras medel till tredje part.

The overall goal of the FED project is to increase revenues and marketable volumes and create or retain jobs for 100 SME enterprises, 50% of which will be women owned. This will be done via three inter-linked activities namely:
1) delivering sector wide trainings (SWTs) to selected SMEs; 2) providing customised business and technical assistance for selected SMEs; and 3) improving access to finance for selected SMEs.
When combined, these activities improve the efficiency, profitability and growth of food processing SMEs and contribute to a stronger and more inclusive sector. Tentatively TechnoServe has indicated that it will work with SMEs that are primarily from Lusaka, Central, Copperbelt and Eastern provinces. However, assessment of clusters of maize and cassava processors in North-Western and Southern (Livingstone) provinces will also be considered. The actual geographical area of operation will be decided during the inception period of 6 months.
The agreement partner is TechnoServe is a not-for-profit international development organization with its headquarters in the USA and a country office in Zambia.
The budget for the proposed intervention is SEK 36Million. The project will run for three and a half years (42 months), including an inception phase of six months. There will be no forwarding of funds to third parties.

External factors significantly influenced project outcomes, shaping productivity and profitability. Past instability of the Zambian Kwacha raised raw material costs and squeezed profit margins as SMEs struggled to adjust prices. The anthrax outbreak from September 2023 to January 2024 halted meat and dairy operations due to government bans, stalling production and sales. Additionally, the 2023/2024 drought caused severe raw material shortages while daily power outages disrupted operations. High fuel costs further strained businesses. The challenges limited production capacity, market penetration, and financial performance.
Objective 1: Improving the Sustainability, Productivity, and Profitability of SMEs/SGBs in Food Processing
Revenue growth: 61 SMEs, including 26 women-led businesses, recorded increased sales revenues out of the targeted 75. Overall, the FED achieved 81% of the revenue growth target, with micro enterprises increasing sales by 61% and small enterprises by 42%. The increase in revenue was attributed to clients adopting new sales and distribution techniques. One of the most successful cooperatives of the project was Kazungula Dairy which increased its revenue by 68.2% in 2023.
Increased production: 57 businesses (27 women-led) increased production, representing 76% of the target (75).
Job creation: 272 new jobs (154 male, 118 female) were created, including 172 positions for youth.
Sector-wide training (SWT): In addition to conducting CTA, the project also facilitated a number of SWTs which targeted businesses in the wider food processing sector beyond the clients that applied to receive one-on-one training and mentorship. 151 SMEs completed SWTs on food laws, regulation, compliance, and access to finance, exceeding the target by 216%.
In-kind grants and finance: FED awarded in-kind grants to 86 of 103 eligible clients, totaling ZMW 6,856,931 (SEK 2,731,945). Businesses demonstrated their commitment to the CTA process prior to receiving grants which were tailored to enhance certification, market access, or production capacity. Three clients secured third-party financing, totaling ZMW 8,262,907 (SEK 3,259,815).
Market Access: Through increased branding and marketing, clients were able to access new markets as well as use new routes to markets. A total of 85 SMEs (35 women-led and 5 youth-led) penetrated new markets domestically and regionally, primarily business-to-consumer sales. Five businesses expanded into export markets.
Certification: A number of products of FED clients were commanded by a mandatory standard. These businesses required a permit from the Zambia Compulsory Standards Agency (ZCSA) in order to sell their products on the market, which many were unaware of. To avoid the companies from having their products pulled from the market, FED provided ZCSA with the names of the clients that were receiving CTA and which were to be certified by the project. 23 SMEs (6 women-led) achieved certification from Zambia Bureau of Standards (ZABS) and ZCSA, representing 58% of the target (40).
Adoption of Improved Practices: The diagnostics exercise found that the majority of businesses did not understand how to forecast production, calculate the break even point (BEP) and determine pricing. As such, many were not receiving discounts from buying inputs in bulk. The lack of forecasting also led to poor cash-flow management as many small inputs were regularly bought on an ad-hoc basis. Targeting the issue, through the training and mentorship provided, 85 SMEs adopted improved business practices and technologies, achieving 113% of the target. Through the training provided by the business advisory unit, clients also developed marketing strategies which aligned with their growth plans.
Objective 2: Enhancing the Performance of Women-Led Food Processors
Mentorship and practice adoption: FED offered female clients a mentorship programme tailored to improve business prospects by assisting women business owners and managers overcome some of the aversions and prejudices experienced by women in leadership positions. The mentorship covered three main areas: (i) improving leadership and management skills; (ii) increasing levels of confidence, and (iii) developing and maintaining professional networks. I addition, 35 women-led businesses adopted improved technologies and management practices meeting 100% of the target.
Business growth: 29 women-led businesses improved sales, access to finance, and operational practices (83% of the target). Notably, Monze District Women's Association (DWA) experienced a slight drop in their sales in 2023 from the baseline of 2022 (at 8.6%). Sales continued to decrease in 2024 due to the increase in power outages in the country.
Indirect beneficiaries: 1,802 women were engaged as suppliers, enhancing women's participation across the value chain, outperforming the target by 360%. Major progress for women-owned businesses were notable in processing companies such as WildHive, Nature's Nector and Wuchi Wami, despite bee-keeping being a culturally sensitive agricultural product for women to undertake, particularly in rural areas. Gender responsive initiatives facilitated the integration of 73 women into traditionally male-dominated roles, surpassing the target by 121%.
Objective 3: Strengthening Market Systems and Service Providers
Partnerships and capacity building: The project formalized collaboration, for example with ZABS, Zambia Development Agency (ZDA), and Zambia Cooperative Foundation (ZCF) through MoUs enhancing market access, certification processes, and cooperative development. A letter of engagement with ZCSA outlined the CTA for certification support. Moreover, in September 2024, FED conducted a finance fair which linked 12 financial institutions with over 200 SMEs.
Advocacy and policy engagement: Three advocacy forums were held on food laws and regulations, business cost validation (with Zambia Association of Manufacturers/ZAM), and a financial fair linking SMEs with financial institutions and government stakeholders.
No indicator available - only a description of the activity results is published
